questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial to me that the institution had a lot of opportunities for extra curricular activities and beautiful surroundings and nature. Furthermore, it was very important to me that the destination that I chose had a big international environment and was rich on culture. Lastly, I found it very important that the institution offered classes in my area of studies that I found interesting.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The application process is very confusing and difficult to navigate in, especially working with UCPH administration, but hang in there, it is a lot easier when you arrive in the UW and the administration at UW are always ready to help.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Somewhat easy. If in doubt you can always email the office of international students at UW and they will help you out,

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The school have different organisations that help new international students and organize events so you can meet other international students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of different opportunities for on campus housing. I lived at the dorms in a cluster. I had one roommate and then shared the cluster (livingroom and bathrooms) with 8 other girls.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There are dining halls and district markets where you can use your meal plan card, other than that shared kitchen facilities are available at some on campus housing buildings

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is great to live on campus as you do not have to worry about commuting and you get to know campus very well. However, living on campus is quite expensive and the opportunity to cook for yourself is very limited.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is a very easy step by step process and if you are ever in doubt you can ask and UW will help you

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: ISS - international student services are always very helpfull

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes that I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register for more classes than you need to take. Do this because in the first week you can drop classes you do not want, but then you have the opportunity to decide instead of ending in the situation where all the classes you want are fully booked.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses are very reasonable.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There are a lot more assignments in the classes that I took at UW then at UCPH. However, the difficultness level is a bit lower and the assignments are also smaller.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Environmental Health In Media (ENV H)
Managing the Health Risks of Climate Change (GH / ENV H)
Contemporary Social Movements (SOC)
Media and Society (SOC)
Comparative Politics (POL S)
Race, Identity, And The Ancient Mediterranean World (CLAS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Race, Identity, And The Ancient Mediterranean World (CLAS) - If you like the classical world and critical thinking about race, identity and how we see and understand the world today.

Contemporary Social Movements (SOC) - This class is really interesting if you are interested in social movements, how they are formed and how they affect political systems.

Comparative Politics (POL S) - This class goes really well with the class Contemporary Social Movements. In this class you cover the various political systems and how they work and how they affect culture and society. 

Media and Society (SOC) - This class is really interesting if you are curious about how media affect society, but also how society affect media and how everything is intertwined.

questions.answer: Insurance, transportation card, emergency backpack etc. that you have to buy when you live on campus

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The food and housing is very expensive in Seattle. I lived in the on campus housing, which is not much cheeper than finding your own housing off campus.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost all sports you can think of is available at UW. Other than that there is a big gym with basketball courts, climbing walls, a pool etc. You can also rent gear from the gym like for example tennis rackets, kayaks, bikes, or even skiing gear.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the IMA and do whatever sport you like or registrer for classes at the IMA like yoga. I would also recommend UWild Adventures if you like hiking or signing up for a team like the volleyball team.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: FUITS and other organisations arrange a lot of different trips and hikes in the weekends that you can sign up for. I also recommend going out and seeing the beautiful nature in Washington State, you can for example take the ferry to Bainbridge Island or rent a car and go to Forks, Hoh Rainforrest, La push, the Olympics, the North Cascades etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to your classmates. People are always very friendly and keen on meeting new people, sometimes you just have to take the first step.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very talkative and friendly.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Keep an open mind and interact with your peers 
2. Sometimes it can be difficult to adjust a new culture and city, but it will quickly get better
3. Bring a raincoat and hiking boots

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Use
www.ratemyprofessors.com
before choosing classes if you want to look at reviews of the professor whose class you are thinking of choosing.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and making friends from all over the world and learning and living in another cultural setting.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adapting the new settings and way of studying

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
